taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: most flowering stems 50 cm to 90 cm high, as in the photos.

traits.height_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: in favourable situations and seasons many erect stems up to 4 feet (1.2 m) in length.

traits.life_span.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: produces from the base many erect stems, year after year: a perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: herbs or shrubs; this species herbaceous, its stems from the base (p. 811).

traits.rosette.note: A basal tuft of grey-green leaves at the foot of the stems, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 80732382, 344281358, 119081243, 159439332, 158669788, 103973336, 67211816, 72133076): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.cauline_leaves.note: Stem leaves fewer and smaller than the basal ones, in pairs, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 80732382, 344281358, 119081243, 159439332, 158669788, 103973336, 67211816, 72133076): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: leaves opposite, the upper ones sessile.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: cauline leaves narrowly lanceolate to lance-oblong: simple.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: leaves entire.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 4 cm to 10 cm long, the basal ones longest.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 8 mm to 2 cm wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: cauline leaves narrowly lanceolate to lance-oblong.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: leaves entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: herbage glaucous, glabrous.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: herbage glaucous; sRGB by eye from the photos (blue-grey green).

traits.inflorescence.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: flowers paniculate.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: corolla 15 to 20 mm long.

traits.flower_colour.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: corolla rose magenta; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 807), Penstemon parryi: corolla broadly funnelform, with a broad flaring limb, glandular.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: corolla 2-lipped.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: corolla 2-lipped.

traits.stamens.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: 4 fertile stamens.

traits.staminodes.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: a fifth stamen sterile (the staminode); bearded in this species (p. 807).

traits.fruit_type.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 806), Penstemon: fruit a septicidal capsule.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: 1,500 to 5,000 feet, mountain canyons and well-drained slopes, spring; March to May here.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripen in May and June.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: 1,500 to 5,000 feet: about 460 m.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: 1,500 to 5,000 feet: about 1,520 m.

traits.light.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: well-drained slopes and canyons, in the open.

traits.moisture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 811), Penstemon parryi: mountain canyons and well-drained slopes: dry slopes and moister canyon floors.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a basal tuft of blue-grey lanceolate leaves sending up several tall, slender stems hung with rose-magenta funnel-shaped flowers.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for Parry's penstemon from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of small-flowered penstemon (penstemon-procerus); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.7 m tall at 3 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
